title: The aim
text: Trap the other king so that it is attacked and cannot escape. That is checkmate, and it ends the game.

title: Setting up
text: Each player has a white square in the near right corner. Rooks in the corners, knights beside them, then bishops. The queen stands on the square of her own colour and the king takes the one left. Pawns fill the row in front. White moves first.

title: How the pieces move
text:
Rook: any distance in a straight line. Bishop: any distance diagonally. Queen: either. King: one square in any direction. Knight: two squares one way and one to the side, and it alone may jump over pieces.

Pawn: one square forward, or two on its first move. It takes one square diagonally forward, never straight ahead.

title: Three special moves
text:
Castling: if the king and a rook have not moved, nothing stands between them and the king is not in check or passing through an attacked square, the king moves two squares toward the rook and the rook hops over it.

En passant: a pawn that has just moved two squares past your pawn may be taken as if it had moved one, on your very next move only.

Promotion: a pawn that reaches the far row becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight.

title: Check and the draws
text:
A king under attack is in check, and the check must be answered at once: move the king, block, or take the attacker. You may never leave your own king in check.

If the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, it is stalemate: a draw. So is the same position three times, or agreement.
